decision_points.question: how are the two raters combined into a single skin-tone exposure measure?
decision_points.why_rival: each produces the skin-tone score from rater1/rater2 a different way (average, min, max, sum, per-rater), and an analyst commits to one construction

decision_points.question: in what functional form does the skin-tone score enter the model — continuous or dichotomized, and where cut?
decision_points.why_rival: each codes the same score as continuous, median-split, extreme-cut, or a swept cutoff; you pick one coding for the primary fit

decision_points.question: on what scale does the continuous skin-tone predictor enter the model?
decision_points.why_rival: standardizing, multiplying by 10, or halving are mutually exclusive rescalings of the same continuous predictor

decision_points.question: which continuous control covariates are z-scored/standardized?
decision_points.why_rival: each names a standardization scheme (a chosen subset, games only, height/weight) for the model's covariates; they never co-occur, consistent with one scheme per run

decision_points.question: is statistical significance assessed one-sided or two-sided?
decision_points.why_rival: reporting a halved one-sided p-value versus a two-sided p<0.05 cutoff are competing directionality conventions for the same test

decision_points.question: what is the unit of analysis / row granularity of the analytic table?
decision_points.why_rival: collapsing to one row per player, per referee, or per referee-country are alternative aggregation levels for the same data

decision_points.question: how are the regression standard errors computed?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice for the SE/clustering slot

decision_points.question: is the adjusted model stratified by league?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice for whether to fit one model per league versus pooled

decision_points.question: which moderation model specification is estimated?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a different interaction spec (individual+club, categorical+club on bookings, individual-only); an analyst runs one primary moderation

decision_points.question: how is the continuous skin-tone effect translated into a reported effect estimate?
decision_points.why_rival: an average marginal effect versus a standardized risk difference at fixed reference values are rival ways to summarize the same fitted effect

decision_points.question: how is the bookings/cards outcome constructed?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice for combining card types into an outcome score

decision_points.question: how is the referee bias (IAT) score coded?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice for coding the bias-score variable (dichotomize at the mean)

decision_points.question: what summary metric evaluates model performance?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice (Brier score) for the performance-metric slot

decision_points.question: is club-average skin tone included as a covariate?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice for adding the club-average tone control

decision_points.question: is a referee rater score added as its own model block?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice for including the referee-rater block

decision_points.question: how wide is the analytic sample with respect to skin-tone missingness?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice to widen to all rows with a non-missing skin-tone score

decision_points.question: how is covariate missingness handled in defining the sample?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice (complete-case on bias score and height) for covariate-missingness sample definition

decision_points.question: is the sample restricted by red-card incidence?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice to restrict to games with at least one red card

decision_points.question: how is the crude group difference tested without adjustment?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice (two-proportion z-test) for the unadjusted main-effect test

decision_points.question: how is covariate balance across groups checked?
decision_points.why_rival: sole recorded choice (two-sample t-tests on games/yellowCards/age) for the balance-check slot
